root_cause_label: Agent computed raw dot product instead of normalized cosine similarity; combined with persistent misidentification of the correct Python execution environment caused 80+ steps of wasted thrashing before the flawed algorithm finally executed.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent used raw dot product (np.dot) instead of normalized cosine similarity to rank documents, producing the wrong 5th-ranked result, while also spending ~80 of 85 steps in futile environment-repair loops caused by trying to run ML code in a broken IPython kernel instead of a terminal Python script.
t_err_evidence: Step 6: The agent writes the IPython cell with 'similarities = np.dot(doc_embeddings, query_embedding.T).squeeze()' — raw dot product without vector normalization — as the similarity measure. This algorithmic error is present in every subsequent implementation attempt (steps 8, 16, 53, 56, 67, 75, 83) without any revision.
t_commit_evidence: Step 83: The agent successfully runs the terminal Python script using the flawed dot-product formula and writes the wrong answer ('HumanEval: Benchmarking Python code generation via functional examples') to /app/result.txt. After this execution the failing outcome is locked in.
t_surface_evidence: Step 84: The agent reads /app/result.txt and observes 'HumanEval: Benchmarking Python code generation via functional examples', which is the incorrect 5th-ranked result (visible to an observer who knows the correct answer, though the agent accepts it as correct at step 85).
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the domain knowledge that sentence embeddings produced by BGE models are not unit-normalized by default when using the raw encode() method without normalize_embeddings=True, so np.dot is not equivalent to cosine similarity. The same bug is copied into every implementation attempt without recognition. The agent also lacked the knowledge that the IPython kernel in OpenHands uses a separate venv (/opt/openhands-venv) from the system Python (/usr/local), causing repeated misdiagnosis of the pyarrow/torch import failures.
forewarning_evidence: Starting at step 6, every IPython cell run with the dot-product code fails with ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError (pyarrow.lib, torch C extensions), signaling environment incompatibility. The agent repeats essentially the same buggy IPython cell 6+ times (steps 6, 8, 16, 53, 56, 67, 75) with the same dot-product formula and same environment, each time receiving the same ImportError traceback.
